title: No reminder notification before end of free trial
body:
I cannot give a review about the application itself since I have not used it. 
But I have had a very unfortunate experience.
One of the main reasons I went through with a free trial was because they said there would be a reminder 2days prior to billing. With our type of affliction, you know, we’re impulsive and forgetful I needed this reassurance so as not to be worried about billing going through. I could simply cancel when the reminder would come up.
However it did not. No email, no notification.
Long story short, I’ve been in contact with Apple and the contact for this application to get a refund. It was very confusing and stressful and either one was blaming the other about blocking the refund.

There is either a fault in the app about the end of free trial notifications or they are simply dishonest. After my email exchanges I am honestly not sure what to think but I shall not be doing this again.

Reminder that EU law states that a purchase can be cancelled within 14 days. It also states that if the seller (in this case Apple) doesn’t mention this during the purchase, the 14 days can be extended to a year.

title: Doubted it, shouldn’t have.
body:
Loved the points at the beginning to get be into playing and decorating.
As time went on, seeing the cub evolve as you level up creates more motivation. 
Love the room being decorated as I like.

Didn’t realize how useful this would be. I rely on “cub” heavily and is one of the first things I check into in the morning with my coffee. 

It took a while to get all the chores in there that I needed reminders for and set to the right intervals (which I love how customized it is able to be).  The breakdown into morning / afternoon / evening really helps with organizing the day without seeming to daunting - being able to see the entire day and then into its sections is really helpful for me. The item I check off moving to the bottom and only leaving open tasks is a life changer. 

The mood log, reflection journals, lessons and quizzes, tools and daily quotes are all items I use. Educational, fun and like being able to look back on my mood log. 

I do not have a enough good things to say. 
The more I use it, the more I discover. At this point it is an open app on my phone all the time. A sense of security reducing anxiety being able to check in and know where I’m at for the day and what’s coming.  It’s also great for looking back on days you feel you’ve accomplished nothing - or what your brain thinks is nothing - but I have an entire list checked off in front of me showing me I was productive. 

I could go on and on - this has been a welcome addition to my journey. I’ve been using for a couple months now and am so happy I gave it a shot. I was very uncertain about it, didn’t think it would help or work - this is an instance I will happily say I was wrong. 

If I have one tip for consumers - don’t be afraid to put in a task you think is “so small” it’s ridiculous to list. If it is something you forget or would like to do more consistently, just add it to your routine. I find I’m still adding/changing mine. Those little tasks get done, you feel good about it. I look around and things I used to let slide no longer slide and allows a more peaceful relaxing environment. 

I’ve rambled enough - but you get the point. If you know you know and get the app because I still can’t get over how incredibly useful and beneficial “cub” is to my day to day life (btw - love I got to customize cub and name, etc).

title: ADHD vs Free Trial Challenge
body:
Having ADHD, free trial periods can be less of a blessing and more of a curse. If I get distracted and miss days, I’m less likely to go back to something. It’s also harder for me to intentionally get into something new or create new routines. The “ADHD tax” (aka where your ADHD makes it way easier to forget to do things like cancel free trials and then end up paying money for something you don’t use later) is also a big problem. 

Because I have ADHD and didn’t get back to this app before my free trial was up, I never got to explore the app to see if this program -that’s supposed to be designed to help with problems I face with ADHD- would even be a good fit. There are no do-overs, no resets. If I wanted to explore the app now, I can’t do so without paying a large weekly fee or signing up for a larger fee/longer plan. I’m not saying it’s unfair or that having ADHD should get people special treatment. But an app designed to help with ADHD should maybe consider this is a problem for a large portion of their target audience.

Maybe the app is great for people like 
me, maybe it’s not. I’ll never know now.

title: Just meh
body:
I was expecting a lot more from this app. I'm more disappointed in it than I thought I would be at first. 

Pros: 
Cute panda

Easy to add goals

Easy to add sub-goals

Handy to open whenever I need to add something vs. needing to write it down in a planner

Cons:

If you don't complete a goal & don't have it set to repeat daily, it doesn't automatically stay on your list the next day. You have to re-add it every day or set it to repeat, & then delete it after you complete it. 

There is no interaction with the panda. It's cute, but it can't interact with you or any of the objects. It just sits there, so it's hard to actually care about it. I was hoping it would be more like taking care of a nano pet/tamagotchi. 

What you can spend bamboo on to buy things for the panda is extremely limited. How many beds, doors, windows, or chairs does one room need? It would be better if you could dress it clothes or give it snacks. 

It's a little buggy. I changed my panda's name, yet the notifications keep coming in with the old name. The challenge where you get treasure chests for finishing goals hasn't worked for me either. 

I wish you could easily change subgoals each day. I want to have a category & just change the subgoals, but if the goal repeats, the subgoals repeat too, & you have to manually delete old ones, not just mark them as complete. 

All in all, I don't think it's worth the cost. It's cute & I liked the idea of it at first, but the more you use it, the more limiting it becomes.

I am so excited and have high hopes this will be what puts me on track. 

One suggestion I have: I am a college student with ADHD and I think I, and many other students in my position, would really benefit from an educational aspect to keep us on track as well. Of course, we can add this in and set our own goals for college related tasks, but usually I forget and am easily overwhelmed without a little encouragement. Possibly even a setting where users can toggle on or off whether they are a student and would benefit from education-related motivators (prompts/journals/goals/lessons). 

Keep up the amazing work, I am really looking forward to this journey! :)
